scripts._comment:dev:fast: Dev server for the NO-CHAIN tier. Identical to `dev` but with VITE_RELAYER_URL set to a host nothing serves: Predict (spec 057) and Collect (055/056) both gate on that one variable, so with it unset their tabs hide entirely and their flows are unreachable — the tier could not test them at all. Pointed at a dead port on purpose: a spec that wants those surfaces intercepts the gateway itself, and a spec that does not sees the honest unreachable-gateway state rather than invented data. Never a real gateway.
scripts._comment:dev:e2e: Dev server for the full E2E tier. VITE_BACKUP_CANONICAL_CHAIN_ID=80002 points spec 032's unified backup pointer at the local chain: the canonical network is Polygon 137 in production, and without the override the backup surface would read a mainnet registry from a testnet-shaped build — the cohort-crossing read constitution III forbids, and the on-chain half of the backup round-trip could not be driven at all. The variable already existed for exactly this (abis/backupPointerRegistry.js). VITE_NETWORK_ID=80002 makes it a TESTNET-COHORT build (getCurrentChainId is env-or-PRIMARY, and PRIMARY is Polygon) so membershipChainId() resolves to Amoy = the local node; without it the modal demands a switch to Polygon and the purchase button stays disabled. The JWT is a DUMMY and deliberately not a credential: encryption is mandatory on the create path, and PINATA_CONFIG.USE_PROXY is false outside a production build, so getPinataAuthHeaders() THROWS without one and every wager creation dies before reaching WagerRegistry. Its only job is to let the request be issued so cy.interceptIpfs() can stub it — no bytes leave the machine. Safe by construction: pinataSecretGuard() in vite.config.js refuses any production build that has these vars set.

scripts._comment:dev:e2e:passkey: Dev server for the PASSKEY FULL-STACK tier (.github/workflows/test.yml, job cypress-passkey-full-stack). It is dev:e2e plus the two build-time variables that turn the passkey rail on: VITE_BUNDLER_URLS_AMOY points at the local alto container and VITE_SPONSOR_PAYMASTER_AMOY at the local relay-gateway. BOTH are read at BUILD time by networks.js#passkeyConfig, which is why this cannot be a runtime toggle or a Cypress intercept — with the sponsor URL unset the client never builds a paymaster transport and never issues POST /v1/paymaster at all. Keep the ports in step with the workflow; nothing here is a credential.
